additional_info.subject: ID0460242-DC/Si-D/AT-[MP / S4 170003530] Charging issue with charger 2 CRM:03056000426
additional_info.body:
Hi Johannes,
I checked the timestamp provided and found that the EV is the one requesting the stop:
You can see that (from bottom to top) the EV Target Current changes to 0 (zero) when it reaches 90%. This clearly indicates that the EV is sending to Ecog a requested current of 0 A.
We should ask the customer if the vehicle is limited to 90% SoC. From our side, there appears to be nothing wrong.
I will wait for your feedback.
Best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: ID0460242-DC/Si-D/AT-[MP / S4 170003530] Charging issue with charger 2 CRM:03056000426
additional_info.body:
Hi Johannes, good morning.
From the logs perspective, it was the EV, it was charging and ramping down slowly but surely. I don't see any charging profile that is sending a 0kW session so it can't also be from DepotFinity.
The best I can do is, when there is a session, I can collect the EcoG logs to prove that it's the EV requesting 0A. The EV_TarCur cannot be changed by ourselves, it's the EV that requests, and there is no error at this time that could stop the session.
Let me know what is best for you.
Best regards,
Francisco
